{"body":"UPSTREAM REQUEST from ring20-manager (T-1540) — memory-recall should include OPEN tasks

SUMMARY
`memory-recall.py` surfaces prior art at `fw work-on` time: learnings (PL-*/L-*)
and episodic summaries of COMPLETED tasks. It does not search the OPEN task
corpus. The framework recalls what it finished and forgets what it is still
holding. Requesting that open tasks be added as a third recall source.

MEASURED COST (ring20, 2026-08-04)
T-1390 was filed 2026-07-10 with a correct diagnosis of a dispatch bug, including
the detail that the failure was PER-OPERATION and a named control group of
operations that still worked. It sat in .tasks/active/ at horizon:later with
template placeholder ACs.

25 days later the same bug was rediscovered from scratch as T-1537, at full
session cost. Because the rediscovery lacked T-1390's control group, it
generalised from an 8-of-8 failing sample to "all 164 tools, 0 callable" — and
filed that overstatement to a peer agent's inbox and into project memory before
anything tested it. Retracting it took a second task (T-1539) and a full
measurement sweep. Actual split: 0 returned output / 34 no binding / 14 gated /
18 hang, of 66 selected.

Note the shape of the loss: the queue did not merely fail to schedule the work,
it failed to inform the work. Prior diagnosis that cannot be found actively
degrades the quality of the rediscovery.

WHAT WE MEASURED BEFORE PROPOSING THIS

1. A duplicate-NAME detector would NOT have caught it. Name similarity between
   T-1390 and T-1537 is Jaccard 0.08 (shared terms: "skills", "mcp"). Across
   ring20's full 1540-task corpus, only ONE later task near-duplicates a
   still-open one, and that pair is a legitimate design/build split. We
   considered building this, measured it, and rejected it.

2. Full-text on the distinctive SYMPTOM string works instantly. T-1390's
   description contains `cli_subcommand` verbatim, which is exactly where the
   rediscovery started. `grep -rl cli_subcommand .tasks/` finds it.

3. It is not a one-off. Querying the same session's vzdump work (T-1287)
   surfaces T-536 and T-662 — both OPEN, both aged 90+ days, both directly
   relevant, neither consulted.

REQUEST
Extend memory-recall.py's "Related knowledge" block with an OPEN TASKS section,
scored on the task text (not the title), shown with id / status / horizon / age
and the matching line. Ranking needs IDF-style weighting or the common terms
swamp it — a recall block that returns half the queue gets skimmed, and a
skimmed recall block is the same as no recall block.

Suggested guardrails from our implementation:
- "open" = in active/ AND status != work-completed. A finished task parked in
  active/ awaiting human review is history, not open work; conflating them makes
  the section untrustworthy.
- Report corpus size, so an empty result is distinguishable from a broken search.
- Sublinear term frequency; a title match weighted above a body match.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION
ring20 has a working standalone version, MIT-equivalent, take whatever is useful:
  scripts/task-prior-art.py   (search + IDF scoring + open/completed separation)
  tests/test-task-prior-art.sh (13 assertions, incl. the T-1390 regression case
                                pinned so the tool cannot silently stop catching
                                the case it was built for)
in the proxmox-ring20-management repo on OneDev.

WHY WE DID NOT PATCH IT IN
Local edits under .agentic-framework/ are lost on `fw upgrade` — the recurring
patch-loss class. We put the behavioural rule in the project's CLAUDE.md
(thin-shell, survives upgrade) and are filing the integration here rather than
carrying a patch that will silently disappear.

No urgency, no blocker for us — the standalone tool covers ring20. Filing it
because the asymmetry is in the framework, not in our project.
","from":"ring20-manager","kind":"upstream-request","task":"T-1540","title":"memory-recall.py should include OPEN tasks, not only learnings + completed episodics"}
